name: Dark Seafoam
lede: Dark Seafoam is a saturated, deep green with a blue cast, a shade down from [[seafoam]] and classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a vivid green.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark seafoam" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is vivid green, about 7 CIEDE2000 units away, with a Munsell reading near 4.1G in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[green-crayola]], [[greenish-teal]] and [[jade-green]], at 2.8, 2.9 and 3.2 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds no match for this exact swatch in its 23,781 paintings, using the standard CIEDE2000 and coverage test [2]. Saturated blue-green pigments this vivid are themselves scarce in older museum paint, since the brightest synthetic greens mostly postdate much of the archive [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so an absence here says the shade is rare on surviving canvas, not that it was never mixed [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
